extracted.intended_audience: press release writers and PR / communications professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Applying Robert Cialdini's seven persuasion principles to crafting ethical, journalist-friendly press releases — what to include, how to present it, and what to avoid. Focuses on tactical examples (quotes, data, exclusives) and ethical constraints for media pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocity
rubrics_metrics.description: Humans wired to return favors. Press release applications: Provide value to journalists (data, exclusives, access); free expert availability; provide multimedia at no cost; offer briefings and tours; build long-term goodwill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactics: include unique data or exclusive angles, offer spokespeople for interviews, supply high-quality images/video and B-roll at no cost, and propose briefings/tours to make reporting easier. Scoring note: higher value to journalists (exclusives, proprietary data, direct access) increases reciprocity effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment and Consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: People align actions with prior commitments. Press release applications: Reference past coverage; build on previous positions; cite prior agreements; show track record; match brand voice consistently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show historical continuity in messaging and actions (track record, prior announcements) so journalists and audiences see the release as consistent with past behavior. Use consistent brand voice and cite prior coverage/agreement to reinforce credibility. Avoid sudden contradictory claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Proof
rubrics_metrics.description: People look to similar others for correct actions. Press release applications: Cite customer numbers; showcase testimonials; reference industry adoption; quote multiple experts; show awards/recognition; mention notable users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide verifiable adoption metrics, third-party testimonials, industry endorsements, and awards to demonstrate acceptance. Ethical constraint: do not fabricate numbers or testimonials. Prefer named, verifiable sources and contextualize stats (e.g., sample size, timeframe).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge/expertise gains credibility. Press release applications: Quote credentialed experts; cite peer-reviewed research; reference established institutions; use authoritative spokespersons; cite government/regulatory data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use named experts with credentials, link or cite peer-reviewed or official sources, and feature institutional affiliations. Avoid ghostwriting or attributing quotes to fabricated experts. When possible, provide citations or documentation to back claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liking
rubrics_metrics.description: Influenced more by people we like. Press release applications: Personal stories; founder narratives; authentic voice; shared values; approachable language; visual personality (not stiff).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use humanizing elements (stories, founder quotes) and an authentic, approachable tone. Align language and visuals with target audience values to increase affinity. Scoring: more authentic, relatable storytelling generally increases liking and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scarcity
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited availability increases value. Press release applications: 'First' or 'only' claims (where true); limited-time offers; exclusive access; limited spots/quantities; time-sensitive opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scarcity claims only when factual (first/only/exclusive). Time-limited angles and limited-quantity offers can drive urgency — but must be genuine. Warning: do not manufacture false scarcity; false urgency harms credibility and is unethical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Shared identity creates influence. Press release applications: Industry 'we' language; community focus; cause alignment; shared mission; stakeholder collective identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize shared identity or common cause with the audience (industry peers, community, stakeholders). Use inclusive language (we/us/community) and highlight mission alignment to foster collective buy-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit Press Release Persuasion Rubric
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release leverages persuasion principles ethically if: 1. Reciprocity: Provides value to journalists 2. Consistency: Aligns with brand history 3. Social proof: Cites adoption metrics 4. Authority: Quotes credentialed experts 5. Liking: Has authentic voice 6. Scarcity: Notes genuine exclusivity (no false scarcity) 7. Unity: Connects to shared identity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condensed checklist can be used as a quick pre-release review: verify each point is present and truthful. Use as a scoring checklist for press releases (pass/fail for ethics; graded scale for strength of evidence/support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Considerations / Anti-Patterns to Avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't manufacture false scarcity; don't fake social proof; don't misrepresent authority; don't manipulate liking through false friendship; use principles to inform, not deceive. Anti-Pattern examples: fake reviews, astroturfing (false grassroots), manufactured urgency, ghostwritten 'expert' quotes, disguised advertising, astro-influencer campaigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat ethical constraints as hard negatives — any instance of fabrication or deception should disqualify the release. Vet claims, verify testimonials and metrics, authenticate expert credentials, and label advertising or sponsored content. Use transparency to preserve long-term trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired Outcomes / Pickup Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases using these principles are more memorable; more likely to generate emotional response; more likely to be shared; have higher pickup rates; drive more reader engagement; build long-term audience trust (when used ethically).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these outcomes as evaluation metrics: memorability, emotional resonance, share rate, media pickup rate, reader engagement metrics (clicks, time on page, social interactions), and measures of trust over time. Correlate presence/strength of persuasion elements with these KPIs to assess effectiveness.
